55229.x: A finished video usually passes through many hands, from the first plan to the last round of notes. Feedback tends to arrive as comments about a specific moment or object on screen.
ELBA Corp. was named a 2027 Honoree in Content & Entertainment at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for YouViCo: End-to-End AI Video Workflow, Directed by Visual Feedback.

YouViCo runs the whole video workflow, from brief, plan, generate, edit, review, fix and approve through delivery, on one AI agent platform. Given a one-line brief, YouViCo Agent writes the plan and shot list, generates assets with 20+ built-in image, video, music and 3D models, cuts them on the timeline, and checks loudness, color and clipping before anyone watches.

Notes are given by showing. Clients open one link and draw on the frame, and the agent reads each mark and makes pinpoint edits to that object or area, such as a logo or a hand, without regenerating the shot. Every comment and approval stays in one place through final delivery.

Designed for full automation, the agent works in the background, and only deleting, spending credits and sharing wait for human approval. Built by a media company with 3 million+ subscribers, YouViCo runs on web, desktop and mobile.

55230.x: A child's growth check and an older adult's bone-health checkup have little in common on the surface. Both, however, come down to reading the condition of the skeleton.
GEMSS Healthcare Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for XPLUS microTOMO, a mobile all-in-one X-ray system.

The system integrates four capabilities: real-time low-dose C-arm imaging, rotation-free 3D tomosynthesis, AI-assisted BMD screening for adults and older adults, and AI-assisted bone-age analysis for children and adolescents.

For musculoskeletal imaging and procedures, it provides real-time 2D fluoroscopy. When depth information is needed, only the X-ray source moves linearly to acquire multi-angle projections, without rotating the C-arm around the patient, and the projections are reconstructed into 3D tomosynthesis images available for review within 45 seconds.

Life-stage-specific AI analysis supports different bone-health needs. Hand X-rays of adults and older adults are analyzed for bone-density-related information to support low-BMD screening, while those of children and adolescents are analyzed for bone age and skeletal maturity to support growth assessment and treatment planning.

55236.x: Blood pressure is usually measured with an inflatable cuff wrapped around the upper arm. A reading taken that way captures a single moment rather than a full day.
United Sensing and MediTech Limited was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for πRing.

πRing is described as the world's first cuffless blood pressure monitoring smart ring. Equipped with high-precision PPG, ECG and temperature sensors and an accelerometer, it enables tracking of blood pressure, ECG, heart rate, SpO₂, HRV, sleep staging and physical activity in an unobtrusive ring form factor.

The ring is integrated with Dr. PAI, described as the world's first personalized AI doctor for hypertension management, trained on 100 thousand one-minute segments, each enclosing ECG and simultaneously highly sampled multi-wavelength PPG. Together they deliver a closed-loop service from intelligent symptom inquiry and real-time monitoring to precise assessment and personalized intervention.

Built on 23 years of original research and aligned with IEEE 1708, the international standard for wearable cuffless BP devices, πRing is currently under NMPA and FDA regulatory review. It addresses the needs of hypertensive patients, cardiovascular high-risk individuals, elderly care recipients and chronic disease management populations, offering medical-grade data continuity for proactive health management.

55238.x: Most screens stay where they are put, on a desk, a wall or a lap. Anything meant to be used while walking around has to be carried or worn.
XREAL was named a 2027 Honoree in XR & Spatial Computing at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for XREAL AURA, an optical see-through XR headset.

AURA weighs under 95 grams and is built to make everyday spatial computing wearable rather than a seated, isolated experience. A dual-chip split-compute architecture separates processing by task: the XREAL X1S Spatial Coprocessor, embedded in the frame, handles low-latency spatial display and sensor processing locally, while an external Snapdragon Reality Elite unit manages heavier computation.

This lets the headset support 6DoF positional tracking and hand tracking without a companion controller, and deliver a 70-degree field-of-view display without the weight typically required for that level of capability.

Running Google's Android XR operating system, AURA integrates Gemini AI on-device for real-time, multimodal, conversational interactions rather than relying solely on the cloud. Its developer ecosystem, built through the Android XR Catalyst Developer Program, supports cross-play titles like Demeo across Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, PlayStation VR2 and PICO, extending beyond a single closed platform.

55240.x: Ports, warehouses and construction sites are busy places where large vehicles share space with people and other equipment. Operators in those places have to watch several directions at once.
Zadar Labs Inc was named a 2027 Honoree in Construction & Industrial Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Zadar360° 4D Radar Collision-Warning System.

Zadar360° is a collision-warning system designed for industrial and commercial vehicles operating in complex environments such as ports, warehouses, construction sites, mines and agricultural facilities. It combines multiple 4D imaging radars with a central processing unit that fuses radar data, tracks surrounding objects, predicts vehicle path and alerts operators when an object presents a genuine collision risk.

Unlike optical sensing systems, the radar-based architecture is designed to operate in challenging conditions including darkness, rain, fog, dust and glare. The system is vehicle-agnostic and can be configured for a wide range of equipment, including forklifts, cranes, straddle carriers, loaders, haul trucks, buses and other heavy vehicles.

By providing continuous 360-degree situational awareness and reducing unnecessary warnings, Zadar360° helps improve operator awareness, workplace safety and operational efficiency across diverse industrial applications.

55259.x: WiseJet Co., Ltd. has won a CES 2027 Innovation Award in the Construction & Industrial Tech category for its contactless wireless connector solution. The award winners were announced on November 9, 2026 (U.S. local time).

The award-winning product, the WC6 60GHz Contactless Wireless Connector Solution, is a wireless communication connector module commercialized using WiseJet's proprietary WC6 60GHz wireless communication technology. Its key feature is that it completely eliminates physical electrical contacts while delivering data transmission performance comparable to that of wired connections.

The currently available module operates at distances of less than 2 cm and supports a transmission speed of 10 Gbps per lane. Using a four-lane multi-lane configuration, it can transmit up to 40 Gbps of uncompressed data (4 lanes × 10 Gbps) with ultra-low latency of 7 ns or less.

One of the solution's key differentiators is its ability to fundamentally address mechanical wear and contact failure, longstanding issues associated with conventional physical connectors. The WC6-AiP-eDP, the first commercial wireless connector module specifically designed for display panel inspection lines, was developed to replace the pogo (POGO) pins traditionally required in existing inspection processes.

The product is the world's first commercialized solution supporting 10 Gbps per lane and implements multi-lane communication through WiseJet's proprietary beamforming technology. This enables high-speed transmission of uncompressed raw data between test panels and inspection equipment without image degradation. By reducing contact failures and repetitive mechanical wear associated with conventional pogo pins, the solution helps improve inspection process reliability and lower maintenance costs, according to the company.

Building on its CES Innovation Award win, WiseJet plans to expand the application of its WC6 technology beyond display inspection lines and into a broader range of industries. The company aims to extend its high-speed wireless communication technology to various applications requiring advanced data connectivity, including consumer electronics such as smartphones and smart TVs, next-generation XR devices, smart glasses, and robotics.

To support this expansion, WiseJet plans to demonstrate its technology at CES 2027 at Booth No. 26548 in the LVCC Central Hall. The company also intends to strengthen its global market presence through continued proofs of concept (PoCs) and technical validation with industry partners worldwide.

A WiseJet representative commented, "Innovation in next-generation advanced industries begins with the evolution of connectivity. Winning the CES 2027 Innovation Award is a meaningful recognition from the global market that WiseJet's 60GHz wireless technology can overcome the longstanding limitations of wired connectors, including mechanical wear and spatial constraints."
The representative added, "We will continue to transform the landscape of industries such as display manufacturing, robotics, and AI servers, leading the way toward a cable-free world."

Meanwhile, WiseJet is a fabless company specializing in the design of 60GHz millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless communication semiconductor chips and modules. The company holds proprietary technologies in ultra-high-speed 10Gbps wireless transmission and beamforming, supported by 31 registered patents and eight patent applications.

55266.x: Neowise, a Physical AI company led by CEO Donghyuk Shin, announced on Nov. 10 that its 3D digital twin platform NeoTwin has been named a CES Innovation Awards 2027 Honoree in the Construction & Industrial Tech category, in the awards program run by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA).

The CES Innovation Awards are presented each year to products submitted from around the world, judged on innovation, engineering and functionality, and design. According to Neowise, no major domestic or global competitor in drone- and robot-captured 3D digital twins for construction had previously received a CES Innovation Award; founded in April 2024, Neowise becomes the first company in the field to be honored, just two years and seven months after its founding.

NeoTwin converts 2D footage captured by drones, robots and handheld devices into a fast 3D model within 15 seconds, automatically finds and re-captures coverage gaps, and completes a precise 3D digital twin within an hour. Its core technology combines RTK satellite positioning, an optical ranging sensor and a camera in a single device, extending the outdoor coordinate system seamlessly into GPS-denied indoor and underground spaces. Unlike existing solutions that treat outdoor drone surveying and indoor 360-degree capture as separate workflows, it unifies a single site into a single dataset.

The finished twin is automatically compared against the BIM (Building Information Model) to quantify whether construction matches the design and how far work has progressed. It can also generate a BIM automatically from 2D drawings alone within a day, allowing an immediate response to design changes. Neowise has validated the technology at a multi-kilometer new industrial facility and at construction sites across Korea, and offers on-premises deployment for high-security sites where data cannot leave the premises. Together with a partner that supplies safety-management solutions to about 1,500 construction sites in Korea, the company is rolling out NeoTwin across construction sites nationwide.

55266.cap: Donghyuk Shin, CEO of Neowise | Photo - AVING News

55266.x: "I want to apply this technology not only to new construction and civil-engineering projects but also to closely understand structures that have already been built," said Donghyuk Shin, CEO of Neowise. "In disaster safety under climate change, if we build accurate 3D digital twins of bridges, tunnels, retaining walls and aging buildings and monitor how their condition changes moment to moment, I am convinced we can prevent major accidents." He added, "Even for facilities built 20 to 30 years ago with no surviving drawings, we can rebuild the drawings and the BIM from actual measurements, and the same technology applies to the high-precision 3D digital twins that precision industries such as semiconductor fabs and plants are now looking to adopt."

Alongside the award, Neowise announced its full-scale entry into the image-processing market with NeoSight, an AI ISP (AI image signal processing) technology. NeoSight processes RAW data straight from the image sensor on an NPU (neural processing unit), restoring low light, haze, blur and noise simultaneously with a single neural network. It renders scenes lit only by starlight as bright as day and has achieved real-time processing at Full HD (1080p) above 30 frames per second while running on the NPU.

In a side-by-side comparison under identical conditions with a low-light-specialized camera used by many drone and robot makers, the company said a general-purpose image sensor costing about one-tenth as much, paired with NeoSight, outperformed the product with the premium low-light sensor in brightness, color reproduction and detail by a wide margin. Conventional methods hit a limit because raising sensor sensitivity amplifies noise and washes out color, but NeoSight overcomes this by using AI to lift the faint brightness information still present in the raw data. "We have completely solved the problem of robot and drone vision getting lost in the dark," Shin said, noting that because it beats darkness with AI algorithms rather than expensive sensors, it can be layered as software onto existing cameras and NPUs.NeoSight is offered in three forms: an SDK embedded by NPU makers, a module that attaches to existing cameras and CCTV, and a finished AI camera for drones and robots. Neowise plans to lead with NeoSight into the CCTV, defense and robotics markets, targeting first the areas where darkness has limited operating hours, such as night-time surveillance and reconnaissance, 24-hour unmanned patrols and autonomous indoor flight without lighting.

Neowise developed all three of its core technologies in-house: NeoSight (image restoration and recognition), NeoTwin (3D spatial reconstruction) and NeoSim, a simulation technology that transfers real-world spaces into virtual environments to train and validate autonomous behavior for robots and drones. The site NeoTwin captures becomes the simulator, and the night-time imagery NeoSight restores becomes the training condition. On this foundation, the company's ultimate goal is to build a Physical AI foundation model for the construction and defense sectors. NeoSim already supports Real to Sim and Sim to Real and is applied to indoor autonomous flight; the company also aims to apply NeoSim to training Korea's 520,000 drone warriors and help make the country a drone powerhouse.

Since its founding, Neowise has been selected for TIPS, the flagship program of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups; is carrying out a Republic of Korea Army AX Sprint project and the Air Force Defense Startup Challenge; and has delivered a simulator to the Agency for Defense Development (ADD). It has filed 25 patents, with 8 granted and one PCT international application, and established a U.S. subsidiary in Delaware in October 2025. This month it is engaging U.S. defense, robotics and CCTV customers through the Silicon Valley GTM program of the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development (KISED). The company targets revenue of more than KRW 400 million in 2026, over KRW 2 billion in 2027 and break-even in 2028.

"The CES Innovation Award is proof that the direction we chose after fifteen pivots has been recognized on the world stage," Shin said. "We will make robots and drones see and understand space as well as people do — night or day, indoors or out — and build a world where darkness and unknown spaces are no longer the limits of machines."

55270.x: UNIUNI, a startup specializing in privacy-preserving AI technology, announced that its home safety solution, SAVVY SPACE AI, won a Best of Innovation Award in the Smart Home category at CES 2027. Building on its experience developing privacy-preserving systems that detect illegal filming and safety risks in public restrooms, UNIUNI has expanded the technology into home safety applications.

SAVVY SPACE AI is a home solution that applies Savvy Modular AI, which lets the safety functions a space needs be configured as required. Through the product, UNIUNI presented its vision of "Privacy-Preserving Safety for Every Space."

UNIUNI's savvy1.5, an always-on AI system designed to detect suspected illegal filming and safety emergencies in public restrooms, monitors potential threats, including suspicious radio-frequency signals, while preserving users' privacy and enabling facility managers to respond even when inspection staff are not on site.

The technology began with the question of how privacy and safety can coexist. UNIUNI developed Non-Vision AI, which analyzes non-identifying sensor data, such as distance measurements, without relying on conventional camera footage. In public restrooms, it uses this to detect suspected illegal filming and risk signals such as falls that facility managers need to check.

UNIUNI won an Innovation Award in the Smart Communities category at CES 2025 for the accessible-restroom safety solution "SAVVY Accessible Restroom: Privacy for Differently Abled." At CES 2026, it received awards in two categories — Products in Support of Human Security for All and Smart Communities — for the public-restroom safety solution "Restroomguard Savvy: Privacy-First Community Security AI." The company has continued releasing products that detect suspected illegal filming, falls, screams and other risk signals in public spaces where privacy matters, focusing on public safety.

The 2027 Best of Innovation was awarded to SAVVY SPACE AI in the Smart Home field. At home, the bathroom, bedroom and living room each carry different lifestyles and safety concerns: bathrooms call for guarding against slips and falls, while in a bedroom or living room a person living alone who collapses may find it hard to call for help nearby. Bathrooms and bedrooms in particular must be watched for safety while carefully protecting residents' privacy.

Designed with this in mind, SAVVY SPACE AI detects risks such as falls without ordinary camera video that captures faces or indoor scenes. SAVVY SPACE AI is a product-design approach that configures sensors and AI functions to match a space's purpose and the detection it requires. On this basis, UNIUNI plans to apply the safety functions each space needs within the home and to broaden its reach to various living spaces such as care facilities.

"Operating technology that continuously detects illegal filming and various risks in public restrooms — multi-use facilities rich in diverse data — we have developed technology that saves lives while protecting users' privacy," said Sooyeon Han, CEO of UNIUNI. "I want to extend that experience to the home, where people stay even longer than in restrooms and risks grow, to save more lives." She added, "Every space where people stay must be safe, and that technology must always respect human rights."

UNIUNI has a track record of installing its always-on illegal-filming detection and fall- and risk-detection AI at more than 1,100 public facilities in Korea, where it has detected some 160 incidents and saved real lives, and it plans to expand into care facilities, homes and more.

55273.x: The more an assistant remembers about someone, the more it holds that they may not want sitting on a company's servers. Where that memory lives is the question.
Priver was named a 2027 Honoree in Cybersecurity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Priver AI, a personal AI companion device.

Priver AI is a personal AI companion device and software that store a user's accumulated AI memory on hardware the user controls rather than in a provider's cloud, the description says. Worn or carried as a pendant, clip or wristband, the device captures events through onboard sensors and a microphone and converts raw data into a private event-graph inside a hardware-rooted secure enclave, with a sensor-side privacy boundary that prevents raw camera, microphone and biometric data from leaving the device.

The memory stays coherent across the user's paired devices through cryptographically attested coordination, without sharing raw data, and external AI systems cannot read it unless they pass a hardware attestation gate and cryptographically accept the user's retention and use terms, with per-service transformation limiting cross-service correlation.

A physical control deletes memory, propagating the deletion to connected systems and recording it in a tamper-resistant audit log, and the description says encryption keys are generated in-enclave and cannot be exported.

55275.x: A modern car's dashboard is turning into a wall of screens, each wanting its own feed of graphics, audio and sensor data. Driving all of them at once, smoothly, is a computing problem.
Qualcomm was named a 2027 Honoree in In-Vehicle Entertainment at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Snapdragon Cockpit Elite, an automotive system-on-chip platform.

From Qualcomm Technologies, Inc., the platform is designed to power next-generation in-vehicle digital cockpit and entertainment systems, integrating the Qualcomm Oryon CPU re-architected for automotive workloads, the Qualcomm Adreno GPU and the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU on a single SoC.

The description says it is engineered to support up to 16 simultaneous high-resolution displays, more than 40 multimodal sensors, AI-enabled zonal audio and concurrent multi-OS execution through hardware virtualization.

It targets a 3x increase in CPU and GPU performance and up to a 12x increase in on-device AI compute compared with the previous flagship cockpit generation, and is part of the Snapdragon Digital Chassis solution portfolio.

55276.x: A mixed-reality headset has to understand the room, the user and a stream of virtual content all at once, and do it on a battery light enough to wear. Power and intelligence usually pull against each other there.
Qualcomm received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in XR & Spatial Computing at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Snapdragon Reality Elite Platform.

Qualcomm's next-generation XR platform is designed to power immersive spatial-computing experiences across a range of form factors. Built for premium mixed reality, the description says it combines advanced on-device AI, immersive graphics and improved power efficiency for intelligent, context-aware experiences.

With up to 48 TOPS of on-device performance, the platform can run large language models and vision language models, letting XR systems understand users and their surroundings in real time, enabling natural AI-driven interactions, photorealistic digital content and seamless blending of physical and virtual worlds.

By delivering enhanced visual fidelity, responsive spatial perception and extended battery life in thinner, lighter devices, the description says it expands what is possible in XR and helps accelerate spatial computing for work, entertainment, communication and everyday life.

The description says it supports up to one Ethernet port, seven USB ports and four SATA ports, enabling flexible I/O expansion.

55278.x: Talking to a device is quick until the room is noisy or other people are around, and then dictation turns into a chore. A microphone made for the job changes how well it listens.
Relay Voice Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Computer Peripherals & Accessories at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Relay Q, a push-to-talk voice input system.

Relay Q is a dedicated push-to-talk voice input system that combines purpose-built hardware with context-aware software for macOS, iOS, Windows and Android, the description says. Its close-range microphone is meant to enable reliable, discreet voice capture across different environments.

The description says its multimodal intelligence combines real-time context about what the user is doing with long-term memory of their preferences, relationships and communication patterns, letting it shape the right words for the moment, preserve meaning across languages and route tasks to the appropriate app.
Together, the description says, the hardware and software create a voice interface designed to work consistently across the places, tasks and applications people use every day.

55279.x: When an emergency hits a building, the hardest part is often telling everyone inside what is happening and where to go. Signs that light the way and speak the right instruction, verified by a real person, turn panic into a route.
SafeEVAC, Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Smart Communities at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Lumexus, an intelligent life-safety system.

Lumexus is an intelligent life-safety system that detects and verifies threats, issues building-wide response and guidance, and shares live event information across response parties. It is built on a family of connected signs, including code-compliant exit signs plus supplemental, entrance and intersection signs, each equipped with a camera, microphone, speaker, LEDs and strobes, with events entering through automated detection such as gunshot detection, fire alarm integration and camera alerts, a wake word, or wearable fobs.

Every alert is reviewed by a 24/7 operations center; once verified, the operator initiates the response defined in the facility's emergency response plan, and the system executes it, with signs displaying color-coded states, patterned strobes and green routing arrows while location-specific audio instructs occupants based on the scenario and their position.
It integrates with fire panels, access control, cameras, PA and mass messaging, and delivers a live incident map to emergency communications centers and responders through RapidSOS.

55282.x: Carmakers now buy as much software as hardware, yet they still shop for it across spreadsheets, email threads and trade-show chats. Comparing one supplier's code to another's has had no common yardstick.
SDVerse LLC was named a 2027 Honoree in Enterprise Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for SDVerse, an AI-powered digital marketplace.

Founded by General Motors, Magna and Wipro, SDVerse is described as the automotive industry's first AI-powered digital marketplace built for software, letting OEMs, Tier-1 suppliers and software providers discover, evaluate, compare and source vehicle software in a single structured environment.

At its core is a technical data model spanning more than 180 standardized attributes, including functional domain, safety certifications, operating systems, communication protocols, hardware compatibility and deployment models, which the description says makes software directly comparable across suppliers for the first time. AI capabilities built on that foundation, including natural-language search, specification-to-product matching and an intelligent marketplace assistant, compress discovery and evaluation from months to days.
Multi-level privacy controls enable secure collaboration between organizations, letting suppliers take part in technical evaluations without exposing proprietary information.

55283.x: Walking is the one exercise nearly everyone still does, yet it goes almost entirely unmeasured. A fall or a long spell of stillness at home often passes with no one alerted.
SHOEALLS Co., Ltd. received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in Accessibility & Longevity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for SHOEALLS LifeGuard, self-powered AI healthcare shoes.

The shoes are built to turn everyday walking into continuous health management and added safety. They integrate a battery-free vibration chip certified as a medical device that, the description says, supports balance and motor function, reduces fall risk and relieves muscle pain; energy-harvesting technology that converts walking pressure into electrical energy; and an AI gait healthcare system that continuously collects and analyzes gait data to assess health status and support early response.

Self-powered location tracking and alert functions also help identify and respond to missing-person incidents, falls, prolonged inactivity and other abnormal situations. Despite these functions, the description says the shoes realize "Invisible Tech," keeping the design, fit and weight of conventional footwear.
The platform is designed to support independent living, continuous health monitoring, location monitoring for vulnerable users and extended use by personnel working in high-risk environments.

55284.x: A hearing aid has to make sense of a crowded room the way an ear does, sorting a voice from the clatter around it. Rules written in advance can only go so far when every room sounds different.
Starkey was named a 2027 Honoree in Accessibility & Longevity at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Omega AI+, an AI-powered hearing technology.

Omega AI+ is powered by the G4 Neuro Processor with a dedicated Neural Processing Unit (NPU), the description says, enabling Deep Neural Network (DNN) processing directly on the device. Performing millions of operations per second, it continuously analyzes and optimizes sound for a more natural, adaptive listening experience than traditional rule-based systems, modeling complex real-world environments and making nuanced decisions meant to reflect how people naturally hear.

The description says it extends intelligence through generative AI capabilities in both the mobile app and the fitting software, creating more personalized experiences for users and more efficient workflows for hearing care professionals.

Despite the processing power, Omega AI+ is engineered into a compact, discreet form factor while maintaining what the description calls industry-leading battery life, overcoming traditional tradeoffs between AI performance, latency, size and power consumption.

SWANCOR Advanced Materials Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Robotics at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for PrimeBOT T1, a transformable personal robot.

Unlike conventional robots built around a single mechanical form, it combines bipedal humanoid and quadrupedal modes in one platform: humanoid mode is optimized for indoor environments and human-centered interaction, while quadrupedal mode adds the stability and mobility for outdoor movement and complex terrain.
The description says T1 can autonomously select and switch forms according to its environment and task, so one robot stays useful across different parts of daily life.
Its mobility system supports a top speed of 10 km/h, zero-radius turning, silent movement, bionic stair climbing and slopes of up to 35 degrees.

55286.x: A window lets in light and, with it, heat the air conditioner then has to fight. The same pane does nothing about the stale air on the inside.
UNIPLATEK received a 2027 Best of Innovation award in Energy Transition & Sustainability at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for SOLARONIX Air-Clean Smart Window Film.

The film is designed to turn ordinary windows into energy-saving, air-purifying surfaces, combining two technologies in a single transparent, flexible layer. A roll-to-roll plasma PVD nano-coating blocks about 88 percent of near-infrared solar heat while preserving a clear view, reducing indoor heat gain.

On the room side, the description says its CES 2026 Award-winning g-C3N4 heterojunction organic semiconductor photocatalyst is activated by daylight and indoor light, generating reactive oxygen species that break down indoor VOCs such as formaldehyde and acetaldehyde into water and carbon dioxide.
It requires no filters, no electricity and no maintenance, and can be retrofitted onto existing glass in homes, offices, hospitals and elder-care facilities where clean indoor air matters most.

55287.x: A blood-pressure cuff captures a single moment, and pressure that spikes between readings slips by unseen. Watching it beat to beat is a different kind of picture.
United MINDS HealthTech Limited was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for PAIrWatch, a wearable blood-pressure monitoring system.

PAIrWatch is described as the world's first multi-sensor wearable Tonoarteriographic (TAG) product, enabling continuous blood pressure (cBP) monitoring and closed-loop hypertension management beyond intermittent cuff-based ambulatory monitoring. It integrates the piRing, piWatch and Dr. pi (Dr. PAI) in a coordinated Ring-Watch-AI architecture: continuous cuffless sensing from the piRing, combined with medical-grade cuff-based references from the piWatch, reconstructs TAG/cBP waveforms that capture beat-to-beat dynamics missed by conventional monitoring.

The description says Dr. pi integrates TAG/cBP, multimodal physiological signals, personal history, symptoms and cardiovascular knowledge for abnormal-pattern detection, risk assessment and personalized guidance, while the piWatch provides display, standalone 4G connectivity and real-time alerts. Abnormal changes can trigger calming music and communication with family or caregivers, forming a closed-loop sensing-feedback-therapy pathway.

The description says the underlying closed-loop prototype received the Gold Medal at the 49th International Exhibition of Inventions Geneva, and that PAIrWatch is currently under NMPA and FDA regulatory review.

55288.x: A hazardous worksite that moves from place to place rarely has fixed cameras watching it. Knowing how many people are there, and whether they are safe, is harder when the site has no eyes.
Webuild Tech Limited was named a 2027 Honoree in Artificial Intelligence at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for PanoGuard GX2, a mobile explosion-proof industrial safety device.

PanoGuard GX2 is a mobile explosion-proof safety device for temporary, remote and hazardous worksites, the description says. Dual synchronized fisheye lenses deliver 8K panoramic video with 360 by 360 degree coverage, while edge AI supports personnel counting, overcrowding detection, safety-helmet recognition and smoking- and phone-use detection, with image stabilization and horizon leveling to keep footage stable during movement and tilting.

Alerts trigger local audible and visual alarms, event snapshots and remote platform notifications, and multiple users can view different perspectives through one device while a unified platform centrally manages many devices.

The device supports wireless integration with gas-detection sensors, 4G/5G and Wi-Fi connectivity, 512 GB local storage, two-way audio and SOS alerts, and with explosion-proof capability, an IP66 rating and 10 to 12 hours of battery life, the description says it suits demanding industrial conditions.

Its 0-to-1.6-meter vertical workspace lets it reach from floor level to shelves, and it can understand natural-language instructions, perceive changing surroundings and carry out dexterous, multi-step tasks such as folding laundry, picking up trash, making the bed and tidying tabletops.

Through a partnership with a household-services platform, the description says customers can book the robot as part of a home-cleaning service for RMB 148 (about US$21) per three-hour session, and Quanta series robots are deployed in real homes for month-long stays to assist with daily chores.

Its manipulation capabilities are powered by X Square Robot's self-developed embodied AI foundation model WALL-B, which the description says is equally applicable to industrial and logistics environments.

55290.x: Passwords can be stolen and a face can be copied from a photo, so the search is on for something no one else can present. A pattern of brain activity is about as personal as it gets.
YNEURO was named a 2027 Honoree in Cybersecurity and Enterprise Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Neuro ID, a neural-signature authentication technology.

Neuro ID is an authentication technology that verifies a person's identity through their unique neural signature. Non-invasive EEG sensors embedded in a wearable capture the user's neural activity, and machine-learning models analyze the signals and match them against the enrolled signature, confirming identity the moment the device is worn and continuously while it stays on.

The technology has been demonstrated publicly, with users enrolling and authenticating in real time. Unlike passwords, nothing needs to be typed or remembered, and unlike fingerprints or faces, the neural signature is not externally visible and cannot be captured at a distance.

Delivered as embedded software and licensed to device and wearable makers for integration into smart glasses, earbuds and headsets, it enables device unlock, secure payments and access to protected accounts and systems for consumer, enterprise and government use.

55291.x: Pointing a telescope at the right patch of sky, then holding it there as the Earth turns, has always been the hard part of stargazing. The gear that does it well is usually bulky and takes practice.
ZWO was named a 2027 Honoree in Imaging at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Seestar S50 Pro, an all-in-one smart telescope.

The Seestar S50 Pro integrates a 50mm f/5.2 four-element apochromatic optical system with dual 4K sensors, a 1/1.2-inch telephoto sensor with a 2.8-degree field of view and a 1/2-inch wide-angle sensor with a 63-degree field of view. It carries an automated Alt-Azimuth mount with an equatorial tracking mode, built-in dual-band narrowband filtering, onboard AI noise reduction and astronomical photometry.
The system includes a 10,000mAh battery, 128GB of storage and NFC pairing, and weighs 2.8kg.
It is operated through an iOS and Android app that supports automated GoTo, focusing, tracking, stacking and remote network operation.

55313.x: AI now lets anyone write, compose or illustrate, yet turning a sketch into a real, manufacturable object still demands engineering software, a factory contact and capital. Removing that wall lets an idea travel from drawing to production file.
HILOS was named a 2027 Honoree in Art Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for HILOS GHOST, an agentic design platform for physical products.

HILOS Ghost is an agentic design platform built to open physical product design the way AI has opened writing, music, illustration, film and software. Turning a drawing into something manufacturable normally requires 3D engineering software, a factory relationship and capital, so most ideas never leave the page, while professionals hit the same wall from the other side, waiting weeks on engineering handoffs that strip out design intent.

HILOS Ghost removes that wall, delivering end-to-end design-to-production workflows and helping designers carry a single idea from first sketch through form, material and specification to a file a factory can run.

Customers can choose 15.6-, 19.5- or 23.8-inch touch displays, portrait or landscape orientation, and integrated peripherals for checkout, self-service, digital signage and connected workflows. Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, NFC, secure and verified boot, enterprise management integration, IP44 protection at the head unit and MIL-STD-810G testing support continuous operation.
Within the Engage One Pro G2 family, it lets customers select the right operating system for each workload while keeping a consistent hardware, peripheral, security and management model.

W2 Ultra integrates purification, mineralization and multi-temperature heating in an under-sink system. Its Dual-Tank System (4.5L purified plus 2.5L heated) decouples production from delivery, enabling flow rates of 8.5L/min warm water in Turbo Mode for high-efficiency kitchen tasks, 6.3L/min ambient water for daily hydration and 4.3L/min at 45 degrees Celsius for immediate drinking and beverage preparation.

Dual TDS probes and flow sensors power an adaptive algorithm that dynamically predicts filter life based on real water quality and usage, replacing fixed-timer replacement, while Fresh Water Technology and dual UVC sterilization maintain freshness without user intervention. The smart faucet offers one-touch selection of 45, 65, 85 and 95 degrees Celsius while displaying TDS values, filter life and system status at the point of use.
Its "purification followed by mineral retention" technology retains 9 types of beneficial minerals precisely during filtration.

55318.x: A long climb or a steep descent is where legs give out and knees take the punishment, especially as the years add up. A wearable that shares that load lets people keep going where their body would normally say stop.
Hypershell was named a 2027 Honoree in Robotics at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Hypershell Halo, a consumer exoskeleton.

The Hypershell Halo is an industry-first unibody hip-and-knee consumer exoskeleton for outdoor enthusiasts, professionals and aging adventurers. Unlike hip-only systems, it powers the entire lower-limb kinetic chain: its four-motor architecture actively cushions steep descents and assists knee extension, delivering 1,490W of output while keeping an ultralight 5.73lb frame.

Driven by HyperIntuition 2.0 and a Mixture-of-Experts AI trained on 10,000 hours of motion data, it anticipates intended movement 200ms ahead and adjusts assistance 2,500 times per second for gait coordination. By neutralizing demanding transitions like downhill braking and heavy carries, the Halo achieves a 50 percent knee-load reduction, a 60 percent drop in metabolic cost and up to 42 percent lower heart rate.
With a 20-second AeroFlex suspension system for easy donning, the Halo lets users explore without physical fatigue setting their limits.

55322.x: A portable drive is usually a utilitarian brick that lives in a bag and comes out only when needed. Making it thin and card-like, something that snaps onto a phone, treats storage as part of the everyday kit.
Lexar International was named a 2027 Honoree in Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Lexar MUSE Ultra-Slim Portable SSD.

MUSE reimagines the portable SSD as an elegant accessory, with an ultra-slim, minimalist, card-like form that turns portable storage into a refined everyday companion rather than a conventional tech accessory.

A purpose-built magnetic system creates a cleaner way to carry and connect the drive: a custom magnetic PogoPin-to-USB-C cable provides a streamlined connection to compatible devices, while a MagSafe-compatible case keeps MUSE securely attached and within reach.

Broad compatibility across smartphones, tablets, laptops and other USB-C devices lets users move between devices and locations, and with read speeds up to 1,050MB/s, write speeds up to 1,000MB/s and support for Apple ProRes 4K 120fps recording on compatible iPhone models, MUSE pairs everyday versatility with performance for demanding applications.

55323.x: The strongest permanent magnets rely on rare-earth metals mined far away and tangled in fragile supply chains. Making a powerful magnet from iron and nitrogen instead loosens that dependence.
Niron Magnetics was named a 2027 Honoree in Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for its Iron Nitride Magnet.

Niron Magnetics is the world's only producer of high-performance, rare-earth-free Iron Nitride permanent magnets. Through a proprietary manufacturing process, it combines iron and nitrogen to form Iron Nitride, which it describes as the most powerful magnetic material known to science.

By using abundant, domestically sourced materials, the company makes permanent magnets that do not rely on foreign supply chains and in many cases perform better for industries such as defense, automotive, industrial motors and consumer electronics.

55324.x: Finishing drywall means hours of overhead spraying and sanding, dusty work that strains the body and is hard to staff. Handing the repetitive passes to a machine keeps the pace up when the skilled hands are short.
Oshkosh Corporation was named a 2027 Honoree in Construction & Industrial Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the JLG Canvas RO2330, a drywall-finishing robot.

JLG Canvas RO2330 is a mobile robotic system that automates spraying and sanding for commercial drywall finishing. Using 3D sensing and LiDAR, it scans wall geometry, builds a digital surface model and automatically plans the work before spraying joint compound and sanding Level 4 finishes under worker supervision.
Its compact 30-inch width fits through standard commercial doors and elevators, while an integrated vacuum helps capture drywall dust.

With up to eight hours of battery operation, 23-foot vertical reach and production rates targeted at up to 3X traditional methods, the RO2330 gives contractors repeatable production capacity while addressing skilled-labor constraints, schedule pressure and physically demanding overhead work.

55325.x: Testing a patient's field of vision for glaucoma has meant a bulky machine in a darkened room they must travel to. A headset that carries that exam anywhere brings the check closer to the patient.
RadiusXR, Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health and XR & Spatial Computing at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for InspirePRO, a wearable visual field perimeter.

InspirePRO is a medical-grade wearable perimeter developed by RadiusXR for visual field testing and glaucoma management across the full spectrum of disease, from early loss through advanced glaucoma. The purpose-built headset provides a 0-to-50 dB measurement range under photopic conditions, using 4,200-nit LCD displays and a 70-degree field of view.

It integrates 200 Hz eye tracking, adjustable refractive correction from -7 to +3 diopters, independently adjustable interpupillary distance and an approximately 358 g wearable form factor. InspirePRO also supports HFA data import, letting clinicians preserve and review patients' historical visual field data when transitioning to the platform.
The system is designed to bring clinical visual field testing into a portable format while supporting the measurement range required for longitudinal glaucoma management.

55326.x: A smart home collects photos, recordings and notes, but sending them off to someone else's AI cloud to make sense of them means giving up control of them. Keeping the storage, the compute and the decisions inside the house is the privacy-first alternative.
Shenzhen laticx technology co., ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Smart Home at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the LATICX Home Agent X4 Pro, a four-bay agentic AI NAS.

LATICX Agentic AI NAS X4 Pro is a four-bay, local-first home AI system that combines private storage, on-NAS AI compute, multimodal indexing, permissions and controlled Agent actions. X4 Pro is the system's compute, storage and knowledge hub, while the C1 Camera, N1 Voice Note and M1 Smart Calendar operate as devices that capture or present visual, audio and shared-home context, powered by the agentic intelligence of the core X4 Pro.

Through the LATICX Agent UI (AG-UI), users can search private knowledge, inspect source-backed results, preview proposed actions and confirm data-changing operations, while core inference, retrieval, semantic indexing and Agent execution run locally on X4 Pro. Personal files, recordings, prompts, indexes and AI outputs are not sent to third-party AI models for these workflows.
The system converts scattered personal information into searchable memory and reviewable action while keeping storage, intelligence and control with the user.

55327.x: Keeping a reptile healthy means juggling heat, humidity and light across a tangle of separate gadgets and wires. Pulling all of it under one controller takes the guesswork, and the clutter, out of the enclosure.
SpaceWalker Technology Hong Kong Co., Limited was named a 2027 Honoree in Pet & Animal Tech at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Habilyt 5 Ultra, an intelligent reptile environment control system.

Habilyt 5 Ultra is a fully modular intelligent environment control system for reptile enclosures, addressing the pain points of conventional husbandry setups: cluttered discrete wiring, tedious separate device operation, erratic temperature and humidity swings, absence of remote oversight and steep learning curves for novice keepers.

Built on an 8-core coupler architecture, it allows free combination of lamp groups, heating pads, misting and ventilation modules and smart sockets under unified control, with SCR variable-frequency regulation paired with wireless precision sensors for steady closed-loop climate control and 20-plus species-specific presets for one-tap configuration.

It supports Wi-Fi app remote adjustment, features gradual sunrise-sunset simulation and a vibration-damping structure, and uses a sandblasted anodized aluminum housing with a clear LED dot-matrix display compatible with mainstream tanks in reptile stores.

55328.x: At a blind crossing, a driver cannot see the pedestrian stepping out from behind a parked car until it may be too late. Roadside eyes that spot the hazard first, and warn both sides, buy back those seconds.
Stanley Electric Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Smart Communities at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Guardian Corridor, a roadside perception and V2X safety system.

Guardian Corridor is a bidirectional roadside perception, lighting and V2X safety system built to reduce collision risks between vehicles and pedestrians at unsignalized crossings and other visibility-limited locations. Streetlight-mounted AI cameras and LiDAR detect pedestrians hidden by parked vehicles, building corners or other obstacles before they become visible to approaching drivers or onboard vehicle sensors, and the roadside unit assesses potential conflicts and transmits risk information to vehicles.

Driver Monitoring Systems can determine whether the driver has recognized the hazard and, when necessary, provide alerts through in-vehicle interfaces, while the system simultaneously communicates with pedestrians through adaptive road-surface lighting, directional audio and roadside displays.
The system supports both human-driven and automated vehicles by enabling cooperative safety actions between roadside infrastructure, vehicles and pedestrians.

55330.x: A real pet can comfort an older person living with dementia, but the feeding, the walks and the unpredictability put one out of reach for many. A companion that responds like a puppy, without the care a living animal needs, fills that gap.
Tombot, Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for Jennie, a robotic companion lapdog.

Jennie is a realistic, fully interactive robotic companion lapdog modeled after an 8-to-10-week-old yellow Labrador puppy. Thanks to an array of sensors and microphones, she understands the world around her and responds like a real puppy, answering voice commands with varied sounds recorded from real Labrador puppies and reacting to all forms of touch, from gentle caresses to bear hugs.
An optional smartphone app lets the user program any name, customize behaviors and push software updates. When it is dark outside, Jennie knows not to bark and sleeps peacefully to preserve power.
Version 1.0 of Jennie's monitoring capability will address Sundowning Syndrome, common among seniors with dementia and notoriously difficult to treat.

55331.x: A ship's hull slowly furs over with marine growth that drags it through the water and burns extra fuel, and scrubbing it clean has meant sending down divers. A robot that crawls the hull and captures what it removes does the job without the diver or the spillage.
Yanmar Holdings Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Energy Transition & Sustainability at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the HC12, a hull-cleaning underwater robot.

The HC12 is a remotely operated underwater vehicle (ROV) designed to clean the hulls of large vessels. It attaches to the hull and moves across its surface, using high-pressure water and rotating cleaning discs to remove marine growth such as slime, algae and shellfish.

During cleaning, removed biofouling and wastewater are captured and transferred to a support vessel, where they are filtered and sterilized before discharge, reducing the risk of dispersal into surrounding waters, and operated remotely with cameras for underwater monitoring, the HC12 reduces dependence on diver-performed cleaning.

Regular removal of biofouling helps maintain hull performance by reducing hydrodynamic resistance, which can lower fuel consumption and GHG emissions, and the integrated cleaning and debris-recovery system also supports operators in managing biofouling and its impact on marine ecosystems.
